title: Seven steps behind Death
hook: Savitri walks behind Yama, talking about the good, and Death keeps stopping to listen
carry: satsang: the company of the good

segments.voice: Yesterday: Yama, the lord of death, with Satyavan's life in his noose, and Savitri getting up to follow. Your line was the body dies; the self is not slain.

Yama hears footsteps behind him. He is heading south with Satyavan's life bound in his noose, and someone is following. He turns. Go back, Savitri, he tells her. Go and perform his last rites. You have come as far as anyone can come. She doesn't argue about the distance. She talks about something else entirely. And Death stops to listen. Behind them, in the clearing, Satyavan's body lies still under the trees.
screen: `FOOTSTEPS BEHIND DEATH.` → `GO BACK, SAVITRI.` → `DEATH STOPS TO LISTEN.`

segments.voice: Savitri's first answer is simple. Where my husband is taken, I go too. Then she speaks of friendship. The wise say, she tells him, that seven steps walked together with the good make a friendship. We have walked more than that, you and I. So, as a friend, hear me. Those seven steps aren't just a figure of speech. At a Hindu wedding the couple take seven steps together, the saptapadi, and with them become friends for life. Yama is pleased. Ask a gift, he says, anything except his life. Savitri asks that her blind father-in-law may see. Granted. Now go back, you're worn out. How could I be tired, she answers, walking beside my husband? And she keeps talking: even one meeting with the good bears fruit, she says, and time with them is never wasted. Another gift. Give my father-in-law back his kingdom. Granted. She speaks of how the good are kind even to those who wrong them. A third gift: sons for her own father. Every gift for someone else. Here is the teaching under the road. Hindus have a word for what Savitri is praising: satsang. Sat, the good and true; sang, company. Being near the good changes you. It's why families gather at the mandir or at home to sing bhajans and hear stories like this one. And look who it changes here. Not Savitri. Death himself keeps stopping to listen. She hasn't asked for Satyavan once. Not yet.
screen: `WHERE HE GOES, I GO.` · `SEVEN STEPS MAKE A FRIEND.` · `SIGHT, THEN A KINGDOM, THEN SONS.` · then, large: `SATSANG: THE COMPANY OF THE GOOD.`

segments.voice: Take seven slow steps if you have room, or seven slow breaths where you are. With each one, bring to mind someone good you've walked beside: a grandparent, a teacher, a friend. Let one good thing about them come forward, and decide when you'll next sit in their company. If you pray, or know a bhajan, let it hold them; if not, simply be glad of them.
Sat, the good, the true, and the first half of satsang, the company of the good. Savitri walks behind Death, talking about the good, and asking every gift for someone else. Today's word.
Your line: satsang, the company of the good. Seven steps, and Death became a listener. That's day seven hundred ninety-nine.

howItsDone: In the epic, each gift Yama offers Savitri on the road follows a speech of hers about dharma and the company of the good; Hindus call time spent near the good satsang.
